item: A custody retry-queue line that cannot be read is no longer glued to the next record, dropped unlogged or erased by a rewrite
summary: custody_pending.jsonl is where a custody write that failed at ingest waits, and a full disk or a power cut is what makes a write fail and cuts a queue write short. A line cut short has no newline, so _append put the next record on the same line and both were unreadable (note_failed(4) returned True; read_pending still returned [1, 2]); read_pending skipped any line it could not read without a log record; a line whose bytes were not text raised UnicodeDecodeError out of read_pending; drain's _rewrite wrote the file back from the records it had read, so the unreadable text was erased for good (and an empty record list unlinked the file); and a read error at drain's final re-read read as an empty queue, so the rewrite deleted every record still owed. _append now closes a file that ends mid-line first; read_pending reads bytes under the file lock (parsing after releasing it), treats a line as a record only when it is a JSON object with a positive integer (not boolean, not past SQLite's) article_id, and logs each unreadable line once per process by line number and byte length (never its text), including a line that is not text or is nested too deep to parse; _rewrite keeps unreadable lines byte for byte in data/custody_pending.unreadable (closing a cut-short tail of that file first) and writes them back into the queue instead if that file cannot be written, so no line is erased unseen; a file that cannot be read is no longer an empty queue (read_pending logs and returns no records; drain's first read returns at once with queue_read_error; drain's final re-read leaves the file as it is and reports queue_read_error). 41 test cases drive the real note_failed/read_pending/drain against real files (10 of the 19 added by the first read fail on the first pushed version, 6 of the 9 added by the second on the next); 48 mutants of the new logic, 48 killed. Limits: a queue holding only unreadable lines is not rewritten (drain_owed and drain return early on no records), so the line stays in the queue file and is reported once per process; the unreadable file is plaintext like the queue and is read by no code path; while the queue's replace keeps failing every drain appends one more copy of the lines to the side file; a text, boolean or float article_id, a lone CR or form feed between records and a UTF-16 line change from base on a hand-edited file only; pending_count still reads an unreadable queue as 0 and, with the Chain of custody tab, leaves out unreadable lines (proposal wal-lane/proposal-custody-unreadable-count-2026-10-29.md); nothing observed in the field.
